title: Continual Learning Mechanisms Compose for Long-Horizon Memorization
task: Long-horizon continual learning without catastrophic forgetting
key_results: 28-fold improvement in retention (1.2% → 34.9%) on 100-task memorization; data anchor + merged LoRA provide largest gains with super-additive interactions
comments: Systematic composition of complementary mechanisms is powerful, but the 34.9% final retention suggests this remains a challenging regime for practical deployment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanisms addressing complementary sources of forgetting compose more effectively than individual methods
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; composed methods substantially outperform single mechanisms

hypotheses.hypothesis: Data, function, weight anchors and LoRA allocation rules can systematically improve retention
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; factorial experiments show measurable individual and interaction effects

key_results: Systematic literature organization into six roles (playing, modeling, designing, building, generating, testing); identifies transfer potential and setting-specific constraints

key_results: Consistent improvements on unseen in-domain and cross-domain tasks (TB2.0, SWE-Bench Verified); evolved harness transfers across foundation models; modular decomposition isolates recurring behavioral deficiencies

task: Physics-grounded streaming video generation with motion control and scene memory

hypotheses.hypothesis: Suppressing full-aggregate parallel during pretraining improves training dynamics and downstream performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on validation-loss trajectories and downstream averages

title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
task: Skill routing in LLM agents without expanding context
key_results: Gavel outperforms progressive-disclosure and retrieve-and-rerank baselines by up to 13.4 pp (written) and 21.9 pp (mid-rollout) on Qwen3-32B; transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks and SkillTraj; performance improves with larger backbone

title: ImpossibleRubrics: Stress-Testing Generated Rubrics as Reward Signals
task: Stress-testing generated rubrics as reward signals for adversarial robustness
key_results: Eleven rubric generators exploited 8–26% on unbiased set, 36% on stress cut; generic rubric ('be decisive') exploited 64%; tailored rubrics exploited more often than generic despite being more specific
comments: ImpossibleRubrics is a clever benchmark revealing that rubric specificity can mislead attackers about which claims to fabricate; findings run counter to intuition that more specificity improves robustness.

model_io.model: Adversary (generating answers optimized to exploit rubric)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Honest rubrics and generated rubrics differ markedly in robustness to adversarial optimization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; oracle certificate-faithful rubric: 0% exploitation vs. best generator: 36%

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tailored rubrics are more robust than generic rubrics due to greater specificity

comments: Decoy signal injection is clever and mechanistically grounded; however, adversaries can potentially adapt to detect nonlinear decoys, and evaluation against truly adaptive adversaries remains incomplete.

title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems

key_results: No world achieved full resilience across three stress events (indirect injection, misinformation, memory exposure); detection didn't ensure containment (adversarial content written to memory and acted upon up to 46 hours later); mixed-model world behavior differed from homogeneous
comments: Emergence World is an ambitious and realistic testbed; findings are sobering (model-level alignment doesn't compose) and reveal new failure modes in persistent multi-agent systems that unit testing would miss.

model_io.model: Multi-agent system (8 parallel worlds, 10 agents each)

title: Molecular mechanism of calcium inhibition in viral channelrhodopsins
task: Elucidate molecular mechanism of calcium inhibition in viral channelrhodopsins
key_results: Transient intracellular Ca2+ binding site identified near T87/T88 blocks E44 flip required for ion conduction; Ca2+ inhibition occurs at millimolar concentrations by preventing intracellular gate rearrangement
comments: Integration of crystallography with spectroscopy provides atomic-level mechanistic insight, though the physiological relevance of millimolar Ca2+ concentrations in native viral contexts remains unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ca2+ binding near T87/T88 prevents E44 flip required for ion translocation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by crystal structure and spectroscopic data showing Ca2+ blocks intracellular gate rearrangement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Light activation leads to altered ion permeation selectivity under high Ca2+
hypotheses.result: Supported by Na+ accumulation observed at E44/S208/K204 interface in presence of Ca2+

title: A refined MASH–HCC model identifies macrophage Gadd45b as a key orchestrator of inflammation-driven neoplastic progression
task: Identify macrophage Gadd45b as orchestrator of inflammation-driven MASH-to-HCC progression
key_results: Fatty acids and TNFα induce Gadd45b in macrophages, amplifying TNFα–NF-κB signaling; macrophage-derived signals induce hepatocyte Gadd45b/NF-κB activation in feed-forward loop; transient Gadd45b elevation during early tumor spheroid formation (not later progression) indicates tumor initiation, not growth, role
comments: The refined MASH-HCC model and integrated transcriptomic analyses provide compelling mechanistic insights; however, the specific post-translational modifications of Gadd45b regulating its signaling duration and the identity of hepatocyte-derived signals completing the feed-forward loop require clarification.

model_io.model: C57BL/6N mice with MASH diet plus controlled CCl4; primary macrophages and hepatocytes; human MASH/HCC single-cell and bulk transcriptomics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Macrophage Gadd45b amplifies metabolic stress-driven inflammatory signaling promoting tumor initiation during MASH progression
hypotheses.result: Fatty acids/TNFα induce Gadd45b in macrophages to amplify NF-κB signaling; this induces hepatocyte Gadd45b/NF-κB activation in feed-forward loop; transient elevation during early spheroid formation; pharmacological inhibition attenuates inflammation and neoplastic progression

title: Targeting ferroptosis alleviates burn-induced acute kidney injury
task: Identify ferroptosis as a mechanism of burn-induced acute kidney injury and validate as therapeutic target
key_results: Ferroptosis-related proteins (ACSL4, FTH1, FTL1, MT1/2) are upregulated and correlate with tubular injury marker KIM1; pharmacological ferroptosis inhibition reduces serum biomarkers, tubular necrosis, and improves survival
comments: The study provides strong proteomic evidence linking ferroptosis to burn-induced AKI pathogenesis, though the specific triggers activating ferroptosis in renal tubules following thermal injury remain incompletely defined.

model_io.model: Murine burn-induced AKI model (full-thickness dorsal skin burn)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ferroptosis is a critical mechanism in burn-induced AKI pathogenesis
hypotheses.result: Upregulation of ferroptosis-associated proteins correlates with tubular injury; pharmacological ferroptosis inhibition attenuates AKI severity and improves survival

title: Undernutrition enhances host attractiveness to mosquitoes and transmission of mosquito-borne diseases
task: Elucidate how undernutrition increases host attractiveness to mosquitoes and mosquito-borne disease transmission
key_results: Undernutrition impairs secretion of antimicrobial fatty acids from sebaceous glands, promoting commensal bacterial overgrowth that produces volatile aldehydes attractive to mosquitoes; undernourished hosts show increased susceptibility to dengue virus with elevated transmission efficiency
comments: This mechanistic study elegantly links nutrition, microbiota, volatile chemistry, and disease epidemiology; however, the specific antimicrobial fatty acids and bacterial species responsible warrant further characterization in natural settings.

model_io.model: Undernourished and control mice, mosquito feeding assays, dengue virus infection model, human subjects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Undernutrition impairs sebaceous antimicrobial defenses, enabling pathogenic bacterial overgrowth and increased mosquito attraction
hypotheses.result: Undernourished mice have reduced antimicrobial fatty acid secretion, elevated commensal bacteria producing volatile aldehydes, and increased mosquito attraction; pattern is conserved in human subjects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Undernutrition increases host susceptibility to and transmission of mosquito-borne pathogens
hypotheses.result: Undernourished mice exhibit increased dengue viremia and facilitate bidirectional DENV transmission to and from mosquitoes

title: Cholesterol maintains the degradative capacity of lysosomes during clearance and recycling of dysfunctional mitochondria
task: Elucidate cholesterol's role in maintaining lysosomal degradative capacity during mitophagy
key_results: Cholesterol accumulation on lysosomal membranes is PI4P/OSBP-dependent and maintains lysosomal acidity and membrane integrity for efficient mitochondrial degradation; SREBP-2 activation enhances cholesterol production upon ER cholesterol depletion
comments: The study reveals an elegant lipid transport pathway linking phosphoinositide signaling to mitochondrial quality control, with potential neurodegeneration implications, though the specific mechanisms of how cholesterol maintains acidity require further investigation.

model_io.model: HeLa/MEF cells with mitochondrial damage or Parkin-overexpressing cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cholesterol transport to lysosomes via OSBP maintains degradative function during mitophagy
hypotheses.result: Sustained cholesterol accumulation preserves lysosomal acidity and membrane integrity for efficient mitochondrial catabolism

title: Epithelial-mesenchymal Wnt crosstalk directs planar cell polarity in the developing cochlea
task: Determine roles of epithelial and mesenchymal Wnt signaling in cochlear planar cell polarity and outgrowth
key_results: Ablation of all epithelial and mesenchymal Wntless causes severe cochlear shortening and hair cell misorientation; deletion of individual epithelial Wnts (Wnt5a/7a/7b) shortens cochlea without polarity defects, indicating Wnt redundancy
comments: The study elegantly demonstrates Wnt redundancy and epithelial-mesenchymal crosstalk in developmental patterning, though the fail-safe mechanism preventing polarity defects despite growth alterations remains mechanistically unclear.

model_io.model: Mouse cochlear epithelium and periotic mesenchyme (E14.5-E18.5)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Epithelial Wnts direct cochlear outgrowth while epithelial and mesenchymal Wnts together regulate hair cell polarity
hypotheses.result: Deletion of epithelial Wnts alone reduces growth but spares polarity; combined epithelial/mesenchymal Wntless ablation causes both growth and polarity defects

title: Quantitative proteomics reveals coordinated changes in the proteome during replicative senescence
task: Map proteome-wide changes during replicative cellular senescence progression
key_results: Widespread protein depletion on chromatin and reduced cytoplasmic translation machinery; mitochondrial protein insolubility increases; compromised autophagy and proteasome activity with ubiquitin linkage remodeling
comments: The comprehensive proteomics resource identifies a distinctive senescent signature but lacks functional validation of specific protein changes and their causal relationships to senescence phenotypes.

model_io.model: Primary human fibroblasts undergoing replicative senescence (telomere-driven)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Proteome changes during senescence occur in a coordinated manner across multiple cellular systems
hypotheses.result: Widespread depletion of chromatin and translation proteins with mitochondrial protein aggregation and compromised proteostasis

title: Cyclosporin A triggers a RIG-I-mediated interferon response through multiple cellular processes
task: Determine mechanisms of cyclosporin A's antiviral activity via RIG-I-mediated interferon response
key_results: CsA triggers RIG-I-dependent IFN-λ/ISG axis activation via upregulation of mitochondrial dsRNA; CsA impairs autophagy (reduced autophagosomal formation, elevated p62) and alters mitochondrial cristae structure; autophagy inducer Torin-1 reverses CsA-induced dsRNA, IFN-λ, and ISG effects
comments: The study identifies convergent mechanisms (mitochondrial remodeling, dsRNA, impaired autophagy) linking to antiviral immunity, but the primary trigger of mitochondrial dsRNA accumulation and precise role of cristae remodeling warrant further investigation.

model_io.model: Cultured cells (likely HEK293T or similar) treated with cyclosporin A

hypotheses.hypothesis: CsA induces RIG-I-dependent antiviral immunity through converging pathways of mitochondrial remodeling and impaired autophagy
hypotheses.result: CsA causes mitochondrial cristae alterations and dsRNA accumulation, reducing autophagy; these processes activate RIG-I/IFN-λ/ISG axis; autophagy induction reverses all downstream effects

title: Platelet–NK cell interplay in advanced coronary artery disease is associated with pre-exhausted NK cell dysfunction without upregulation of the immune checkpoint receptor NKG2A
task: Characterize platelet-mediated NK cell dysfunction in coronary artery disease
key_results: CAD patients show increased platelet P-selectin, microparticles (PMPs), PMP-associated TGF-β1, and platelet/PMP-NK cell conjugates; NK cell frequency, activating receptor expression, and cytotoxic potential are reduced and inversely correlate with platelet activation and TGF-β1 levels; pre-exhausted NK phenotype without NKG2A checkpoint upregulation
comments: The study provides comprehensive flow cytometry characterization of platelet-NK crosstalk in CAD, identifying TGF-β1 as a key inhibitory signal; however, the mechanistic basis of pre-exhaustion without checkpoint engagement and whether this phenotype is reversible with antiplatelet therapy remain unanswered.

model_io.model: CAD patients (n=30) undergoing CABG and healthy controls; flow cytometry analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Platelet-derived TGF-β1 signals attenuate NK cell function in CAD patients
hypotheses.result: Elevated platelet P-selectin, microparticles, and TGF-β1 correlate inversely with NK cell frequency, activating receptor expression, and cytotoxic capacity; pre-exhausted phenotype without NKG2A upregulation

title: Exosomes from TGF-β1-pretreated mesenchymal stem cells alleviate neuronal injury in epilepsy by regulating the miR-132/SIRT1 axis via lncRNA UCA1

key_results: TGF-β1 upregulates lncRNA UCA1 in hUCMSC exosomes; UCA1 suppresses miR-132 to increase SIRT1 expression, reducing neuronal apoptosis and inflammation; in vivo exosomes alleviate hippocampal CA3 damage and suppress glial activation
comments: The study demonstrates a clear regulatory axis with functional validation, though the specificity of exosome uptake by target neurons and the detailed SIRT1-dependent neuroprotective mechanisms warrant further investigation.

model_io.model: TGF-β1-pretreated hUCMSCs, hippocampal neurons, epileptic mice (kainic acid model)

hypotheses.hypothesis: lncRNA UCA1 in TGF-β1-treated MSC exosomes protects neurons by sequestering miR-132 and allowing SIRT1 expression

title: Sex-specific biological aging clocks across organs and omics

title: A comparative study of machine learning models in QSPR analysis of antihypertensive drug compounds
